ProgrammingNotes.description:
1. For rows where the number of participants in each analysis set is presented, base the number of participants on applicable participant treatment grouping (eg, use TRTxxP for the ITT Analysis Set or the FAS Analysis Set row and TRTxxA for the Safety Analysis Set or the PK Analysis Set row). Add rows to include all analysis sets specified in the SAP. Use the [ITT][Full] Analysis Set and TRTxxP for the denominator in studies where the [ITT][Full] Analysis Set is the primary efficacy analysis set; otherwise, use the Safety Analysis Set and TRTxxA.
2. Reasons for Premature Discontinuation should match the study eCRF. As a default, categories with all zeros are omitted. When it adds value, all categories as listed on the eCRF may be displayed, including categories with all zeros.
3. Only display "Reason for [Premature] Discontinuation of [Any] Study [Drug] [Treatment]" section if any participants discontinued study drug. Only display "Reason for [Premature] Study Discontinuation" section if any participants discontinued the study.
4. "Continuing Study [Drug][Treatment]", "Continuing Study", and completion at specific time points may be added for interim analyses.
5. Denominator for categories under a treatment phase should be the number of participants who entered the respective treatment phase.
6. Sort the reasons for premature discontinuation by descending frequency under the total column. If the frequency is tied, then sort by alphabetical order.
7. The annotations of 'TRTxxP(N)', 'TRTxxA(N)', 'AREL(N)' and other similar ones in the tables and listings indicate that either the character (eg, TRTxxP, AREL) or the numeric (eg, TRTxxPN, ARELN) variable can be used to create the column or row.

1. ITT or All Enrolled analysis set may be used instead of Safety for studies that use the ITT or All Enrolled analysis set as the primary analysis set. For multiphase studies, [Study Specific] analysis set may be used based on the study design.
2. The following conventions will be used for the imputation of date of birth when it is partially missing or not collected:
  - If only month and year of birth is collected, then "15" will be imputed as the day of birth
  - If only year of birth is collected, then "01 July" will be imputed as the day and month of birth
  - If year of birth is missing, then date of birth will not be imputed.
  In general, age collected at Day 1 (in years {or specify unit}) will be used for analyses and presented in listings. If age at Day 1 is not available for a participant, then age derived based on date of birth and the Day 1 visit date will be used instead. If an enrolled participant was not dosed with any study drug, the randomization [enrollment] date will be used instead of the Day 1 visit date.
  For screen failures, the date the first informed consent was signed will be used for the age derivation. Age required for longitudinal and temporal calculations and analyses (e.g., estimates of creatinine clearance, age at date of AE) will be based on age derived from date of birth and the date of the measurement or event, unless otherwise specified. (Note, see SAP and discuss with Biometrics team).
3. Baseline characteristics (e.g., weight, height, and BMI) are presented in the same table with the demographics.
4. Height, weight, and/or body mass index (BMI) may also be displayed by sex if specified in the SAP. Derived BMI values will be reported instead of the collected value from eCRF.
5. Optional row for missing or unknown category may be added where applicable (e.g., interim analyses) and dropped for final analysis if all zero counts.
6. Categories for race and ethnicity should follow the order in the study eCRF.
7. As a default, categories with all zeros are omitted. If they add value, all categories as listed on the CRF may be displayed, including categories with all zeros.
8. Missing values may be included in percent calculations so percentages should add to 100%.
9. *Use TRTxxA(N) when displaying the safety analysis set, and TRTxxP(N) otherwise.
10. The values of this variable cannot be used directly to satisfy the requirements of the table. An additional variable should be created in the table program to change to case or associate a format so that the display matches the mockup display.
11. Categories for age group and BMI group may be added if specified in the SAP. Up to a maximum of three age groups is permitted in the display.

1. Only present intensive PK sampling data in this listing.
2. A unique symbol with corresponding footnote should be used for each reason for data exclusion.
3. Geometric mean is optional should only be produced at the request of Clinical Pharmacology and is not presented as a default.
4. PK concentration values will be presented as provided and summary statistics will be presented to 3 significant digits. Please research how significant digits are done if you are not familiar with using them.
5. The Population Set may be displayed as "{Analyte}{Intensive} PK [Substudy] Analysis Set" using ADSL.PKFL or ADSL.PKyFL.
6. The by-groups for tables 15.10.1.1.x: and 15.10.1.2.x "Treatment: {GS-XXXX (XXmg)}" may be displayed using ADPC.TRTP(N) or ADSL.TRTxxP(N).

Refer to the TFL Designer 'GCDS Template Instructions' tab, under the 'Data Presentation' heading, for 'Adverse Events Tables Programming Notes'; these notes contain example tables for points 17 and 18, below, with the logic for analysis counts.

GENERAL:
1. The rows presented in the Overall AE Summary table should match the AE outputs presented in the study. A row for Death ADSL.DTHFL is required in the Overall AE Summary table unless a separate Death summary table is presented in the study.
2. If the Overall AE Summary table is generated using a Subgroup analysis, then each category of the subgroup will displayed on a separate page as the first row of that page.
3. For TEAEs of interest, optional rows may be added to the Overall AE Summary table. However, for multiple categories of TEAEs of interest a separate Overall AE Summary table for TEAEs of interest may be used, then each category of interest will be displayed on a separate page as the first row of that page.
4. Use the Safety ADSL.SAFFL Analysis Set for Adverse Event tables.
5. Only TEAEs will be summarized unless otherwise specified; TEAEs will be defined as any AEs that occurred on or after the first study drug dosing date and up to {XX} days {or study drug-specific therapeutic reach} after the date of the last dose of the study drug [and prior to the day of initiation of subsequent anticancer/antiviral/etc. therapy], unless otherwise specified. For interim analyses, refer to SAP for participants who are ongoing on study drug.
6. If the onset date of the AE is incomplete and the AE stop date is not prior to the first dosing date of study drug, then the month and year (or year alone if month is not recorded) of onset determine whether an AE is treatment emergent. The event is considered treatment emergent if both of the following 2 criteria are met:
   • The AE onset is the same as or after the month and year (or year) of the first dosing date of study drug, and
   • The AE onset date is the same as or before the month and year (or year) of the date corresponding to {XX} days {or study drug-specific therapeutic reach} after the date of the last dose of study drug [and prior to the day of initiation of subsequent anticancer/antiviral/etc. therapy].
An AE with completely missing onset and stop dates, or with the onset date missing and a stop date later than the first dosing date of study drug, will be considered to be treatment emergent. In addition, an AE with the onset date missing and incomplete stop date with the same or later month and year (or year alone if month is not recorded) as the first dosing date of study drug will be considered treatment emergent.
7. Default sort order is alphabetically for SOCs [and HLT within SOC,] and then descending frequency of PTs in the total column. Summaries that include PT only, sort order is by descending frequency of PTs in the total column. Optionally, a different sort order maybe specified as based on the study design.
8. For studies that collect adverse event data for individual study drugs, the layout may be altered to summarize the individual study drugs separately.
9. A total column may be presented for studies where different doses of the same study drug are displayed.
10. Rows may be added to summarize the number of participants with missing data, as applicable.
11. Lower severity grades may be excluded from table summaries, as applicable.
12. A P value may be displayed if pre-specified in the SAP. Display P values in a column if 2 treatment groups are shown in the table, or in a row if more than 2 treatment groups are shown.
13. For Oncology studies, refer to the SAP when determining relevant custom grouping for lab abnormality AE terms (e.g., ADAE.AEDECOD are mapped: Neutrophil count decreased->Neutropenia, White blood cell count decreased->Leukopenia, Lymphocyte count decreased->Lymphopenia, Red blood cell count decreased->Anaemia, Platelet count decreased->Thrombocytopenia). Related footnote should be added to explain this.
14. For studies where the analysis is based on the Treatment Emergent within each period, then in such instances the variable ADAE.TREMxxFL can be utilized to summarize the AE’s. [xx] in the variable name indicates each period and will be replaced by 01, 02, 03, etc.
15. Rows for treatment mean difference and P value are optional for Exposure-Adjusted Incidence Rate (EAIR) summaries. Refer to the SAP when determining relevant statistical methods.
16. For Oncology studies, the required displays are separate summaries of ‘TEAE with Grade 3 or 4‘ and ‘TEAE Leading to Death’ (i.e., TEAE with Grade 5) instead of the combined summaries of ‘TEAE with Grade 3 or Higher‘. For Virology and Inflammation studies, the preferred display is the combined summaries of ‘TEAE with Grade 3 or Higher‘ and separate summaries of ‘TEAE with Grade 3 or 4‘ and ‘TEAE Leading to Death’ (i.e., TEAE with Grade 5) are optional only.
17. <Refer to 'Adverse Events Tables Programming Notes' in the 'GCDS Template Instructions' tab>
For Table 15.11.2.1.1 TEAE Overall Summary, the following rows are intended to count participants once only and at the highest severity grade experienced per participant throughout the study:
   • TEAE with Grade 3 or 4
   • TEAE Leading to Death
If the highest severity grade experienced is a Grade 5, then those participants would be excluded from the “TEAE with Grade 3 or 4” row (but would be counted in the “TEAE Leading to Death” row).
For summaries related to study drug, subset records on relationship to study drug (ADAE.AREL=’RELATED’) first, before determining the highest severity grade experienced per participant. Participants are counted once only in the following rows at the highest severity grade experienced per participant of the drug-related TEAEs. If the highest severity grade of the drug-related TEAEs is a Grade 5, the participant is excluded from the “TEAE Related to Study Drug with Grade 3 or 4” row (but is counted in the “TEAE Related to Study Drug Leading to Death” row).
   • TEAE Related to Study Drug with Grade 3 or 4
   • TEAE Related to Study Drug Leading to Death
Example Study: In a 20-participant study, 20 participants have treatment-emergent maximum Grade 4 neutropenia and 2 participants have treatment-emergent maximum Grade 5 febrile neutropenia. All events are considered treatment-related except one case of Grade 5 febrile neutropenia. Refer the following summary table displays the expected participant counts:
18. <Refer to 'Adverse Events Tables Programming Notes' in the 'GCDS Template Instructions' tab>
For Table 15.11.2.2.2.1 Grade 3 or 4 TEAEs by SOC and PT, in the first summary row, include participants who experienced a maximum severity of Grade 3 or 4 throughout the study (ADAE.AOCCIFL=’Y’ and ADAE.ATOXGRN in (3, 4)) and exclude participants who experienced a maximum severity of Grade 5 – this matches the “TEAE with Grade 3 or 4” row in the Overall Summary table. Subsequent rows for SOC, exclude participants who experienced Grade 5 when counting the highest severity grade within this SOC (ADAE.AOCCSIFL=’Y’ and ADAE.ATOXGRN in (3, 4)). Subsequent rows for PT, exclude participants who experienced Grade 5 when counting the highest severity grade within this PT (ADAE.AOCCPIFL=’Y’ and ADAE.ATOXGRN in (3, 4)).
Additionally, for Table 15.11.2.3.3.1 Grade 3 or 4 Treatment-Related TEAEs by SOC and PT, subset the records on relationship to study drug (ADAE.AREL=’RELATED’) first, before determining the highest severity grade (i.e., Grade 3 or 4) per participant (first row – matches Overall Summary table) and for each SOC and PT when selecting records for the relevant 1st Max Sev./Int. and Related to Study Drug Occurrence Flag (ADAE.AOCCzzFL).

DisplaySection.Text: Individual Data and Summary Statistics of Plasma Concentration (ng/mL) at Protocol-Specified Sampling Times
BLQ = below the limit of quantitation; LLOQ = lower limit of quantitation; CI = confidence interval.
Values BLQ were treated as 0 for predose and postdose.
If > 1/3 of postdose values are BLQ at a time point, then the mean, StD, and %CV are not calculated at that time point.
LLQ was defined as 5.0 ng/mL for analyte GS-XXXX.
For each participant in PK analysis set, intensive serial PK sample collection (samples over 24-hr postdose) was performed at Day 1.
